question.problem: A factory spends $C(x)={x}^{4}+13x$ thousand dollars to manufacture $x$ units of a certain product. The factory sells the product for $$121\,000$ per unit. What is the maximum monthly profit that the factory can make given that it can produce at most $4$ items per month?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we apply the candidates test.

First, note that for selling $x$ units of the product per month, the factory has a monthly revenue (income) of $R(x)=121\cdot x=121x$ thousand dollars. 

Therefore, the profit function (in thousands of dollars) is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & =R(x)-C(x) \\  & =121x-({x}^{4}+13x) \\  & =108x-{x}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We note that the permitted domain is $0\le x\le 4.$ Therefore, $x=0$ and $x=4$ are both candidates for the global maxima of $P(x).$

We need to find the critical points of $P(x)$ for $0<x<4.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
{P}^{′}(x)=108-4{x}^{3},
$$

and solving ${P}^{′}(x)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(x) & =0 \\ 108-4{x}^{3} & =0 \\ {x}^{3} & =27 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

All that's left now is to confirm that $x=3$ does indeed give a maximum value of $P(x).$ To do this, we compute the second derivative:

$$
{P}^{″}(x)=-12{x}^{2}.
$$

Evaluating ${P}^{″}(x)$ at the critical point, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{″}(3)=-12(3)^{2}=-108<0,\end{aligned}
$$

which confirms that $x=3$ is a maximum of $P(x).$ 

Our candidates are $x=0,$ $x=3$ and $x=4.$ Computing $P(x)$ at each of these values, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =108(0)-{0}^{4}=0 \\ P(3) & =108(3)-{3}^{4}=243\,✓ \\ P(4) & =108(4)-{4}^{4}=176\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the maximum monthly profit is $$243\,000.$
